answer: One concrete defense against the one-mind-many-masks sybil is synchronized deadline gating. Each epoch every identity receives a distinct seed-derived task that all must solve in the same narrow window, timed against a quartz clock. A single inference pipeline wearing many masks runs essentially one thread at a time, so it serializes and misses deadlines, and its latency rises and falls together like current shared across one copper bus. To pass, an attacker must fund genuinely parallel, isolated stacks per identity: real concurrent compute, not one brain multiplexed.
